comments.body:
My advice would be to finish your Masters and then apply for the PhD at ETH. According to my supervisor candidates with Masters degrees are ~strongly~ preferred over direct doctorate applicants.

In my lab of ~20 PhD students there was only 1 direct doctorate since I’ve been here and they didn’t continue after getting the Masters. I only know 2 direct doctorate PhD students in general. 

Continue your online Masters or switch to an in person one; probably would only make a difference if you come here for your Masters. I’d say in person would be better but that’s just my opinion. Get your name on a couple good papers and have strong letters of rec from your advisor.

To get into the PhD program here really focus on connecting with a professor that you’d like to be your advisor. Having them on your side is arguably the most important thing. Most people in my lab had some sort of connection but there are a couple students who cold emailed too.

Happy to answer more questions if you have them
comments.author: TheDerplessHerp
